name: The Rovere of Vallone San Giuseppe

location.address: Strada Comunale Artemano 6, loc. Vallone San Giuseppe, Piano di Sorrento
location.neighbourhood: Vallone San Giuseppe, Piano di Sorrento

verified_sources: https://www.regione.campania.it (MASAF national monumental-trees register, sheet 13/G568/NA/15, imported at data/registers/italy-masaf.json)
access: Free, public ground. The tree stands beside Strada Comunale/Via Artemano, an ordinary public residential road (confirmed via OpenStreetMap: highway=residential and highway=footway, no access= restriction tagged) that runs within about 20-30 metres of the tree's registered coordinate, on the edge of a small country lane above a stream valley. No gate, ticket or reception desk.
transport: Roughly 1.5 km, mostly uphill, from Piano di Sorrento's Circumvesuviana station; walkable in about 25-30 minutes or a short drive/taxi.
verify_notes: Tall, straight-growing sessile oak (Quercus petraea), part of a small residual patch of oak woodland ('nucleo boschivo di roveri') growing alongside hazels, on the steep left bank of a torrent stream that rises about 50m higher at the springs of Monte Vicalvano. At about 7m up, the trunk forks into two primary branches (described this way in the source book). The clayey soil it grows in gave the neighbouring street names, Via Creta and Via Artemano ('creta' = clay, historically dug here for brickmaking). Two sources: the MASAF national register (sheet 13/G568/NA/15, girth given there as 346cm) and the Regione Campania regional scheda (agricoltura.regione.campania.it/foreste/monum/scheda_46.html, directly fetched, girth given there as 333cm; used girth_cm=333 from the more detailed regional card, but note the ~13cm discrepancy between the two government sources). The regional scheda states the tree is already documented in 'Gli alberi secolari in Campania' (2008, Regione Campania with LIPU Napoli and the Corpo Forestale dello Stato) and gives its age only as 'secolare' (age-old/century-old), a vague real-source descriptor repeated as vaguely as given rather than sharpened into a number; age_min set to 100 on that basis, age_max deliberately left open. Flagged only for the alive-now test: no dated photo, news item or recent observation newer than the 2008 book/register citation was found this pass; nothing suggests it has been lost either, and it stands in a wooded stream-bank setting rather than an exposed street position (unlike this same register's Via Bagnulo pine two sheets earlier, which is documented as having partially collapsed nearby street trees in Aug 2026, see leads file). A future pass or reader could confirm with a dated photo. Not a bridge claim: the century-old age comes directly from the source's own word for this specific tree, not derived from park/planting context.
